# False Positive: First-Party Billing and Service Error Reporting Domains Blocked

This is a false-positive report, not an advertisement report.

## Summary

The AdGuard DNS filter incorrectly blocks several first-party service
reporting domains used by our browser-based service and applications on
Desktop and Mobile.

These endpoints are used for customer service usage metering required for
billing, service error reporting, diagnostics, operational status, and HTTPS
or WebSocket log transmission.

## Affected Domains

- `logreport-global-dual.cool*cloud.com`
- `logreport-global-dual.coolbcloud.com`
- `logreport-global-dual.coolhcloud.com`
- `detaillog-global-dual.coolbcloud.com`
- `detaillog-global-dual.coolhcloud.com`
- `detaillog-global-dual.coolccloud.com`
- `detaillog-global-dual.coolgcloud.com`
- `weblogger-wss.cool*cloud.com`
- `wslog-global-dual.cool*cloud.com`
- `wslog-global-dual.coolccloud.com`

## Affected Rules

```text
||logreport-global-dual.cool*cloud.com^
||logreport-global-dual.coolbcloud.com^
||logreport-global-dual.coolhcloud.com^
||detaillog-global-dual.coolbcloud.com^
||detaillog-global-dual.coolhcloud.com^
||detaillog-global-dual.coolccloud.com^
||detaillog-global-dual.coolgcloud.com^
||weblogger-wss.cool*cloud.com^
||wslog-global-dual.cool*cloud.com^
||wslog-global-dual.coolccloud.com^
```

## Purpose of These Domains

These are first-party endpoints belonging to our own service infrastructure.
They are used for:

- Customer service usage and metering information required for billing;
- Service errors, exceptions, and diagnostic information;
- Service health and operational status;
- HTTPS and WebSocket log transmission.

The data is limited to service-level usage, billing metering, error, and
system-health information. It is not used for advertising, ad attribution,
behavioral profiling, or cross-site tracking. It does not contain users'
communication contents or personal privacy data.

These domains do not serve advertisements or tracking scripts.

## Reproduction and DNS Comparison

The affected domain resolves normally through non-filtering DNS resolvers.

Google DNS returns a regional service endpoint:

```text
$ dig +short @8.8.8.8 logreport-global-dual.coolbcloud.com

logreport-global-dual.coolacloud.com.
logreport-sgp-dual-base.coolacloud.com.
8.219.127.160
```

Another public DNS resolver returns the following service endpoints:

```text
$ dig @114.114.114.114 logreport-global-dual.coolbcloud.com

logreport-global-dual.coolbcloud.com. CNAME logreport-global-dual.coolacloud.com.
logreport-global-dual.coolacloud.com. CNAME logreport-sh-dual-base.coolacloud.com.
logreport-sh-dual-base.coolacloud.com. A 106.14.181.205
logreport-sh-dual-base.coolacloud.com. A 106.14.52.63
```

The different real IP addresses returned by non-filtering DNS resolvers are
expected because the service uses regional DNS routing.

However, AdGuard DNS returns a reserved, non-routable address instead of the real service endpoint:

```text
$ dig @94.140.14.14 logreport-global-dual.coolbcloud.com

logreport-global-dual.coolbcloud.com. A 198.18.0.25
```

When the domain is resolved through public DNS resolvers such as 114.114.114.114 and 8.8.8.8, the service endpoint is reachable and log uploading works normally. When it is resolved through AdGuard DNS, the endpoint resolves to the reserved, non-routable address 198.18.0.25 instead of the actual service endpoint, and log parsing and log uploading fail.

This provides evidence that the observed failure is caused by DNS-level filtering in AdGuard DNS.

## Impact

Blocking these domains can cause:

- Log parsing and log uploading failures;
- Incomplete or delayed customer usage metering for billing;
- Service errors and exceptions not being reported in time;
- Delayed monitoring, troubleshooting, and incident response.

The issue is resolved when the affected domains are resolved through a
non-filtering DNS resolver or added to the allowlist.

## Request

Please review these rules as false positives and remove them from the AdGuard
DNS filter, or add suitable exceptions for these first-party service
reporting endpoints.

The rules can be found in the compiled AdGuard DNS filter:

<https://adguardteam.github.io/AdGuardSDNSFilter/Filters/filter.txt>

We can provide additional sanitized DNS information or connection metadata if
needed. We will not provide access tokens, private logs, customer identifiers,
or confidential customer data.
